html:
SMTO-K8S-0002 — SMTO couldn't confirm it's reaching the right Kubernetes cluster

GUID: a4db97f3-c1b7-45f5-b7fa-fb6a87b3ada8
Slug: kubernetes-trust-unverified
Domain: K8S · Subsystem: k8s

What happened

  • Before remembering a Kubernetes cluster, SMTO checks how your settings reach and trust it. These settings use a connection SMTO can't verify, such as an unencrypted address or a skipped certificate check. Your command wasn't blocked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages Kubernetes access to check that the cluster address in the Gateway computer's Kubernetes settings starts with https://. SMTO only trusts encrypted connections whose identity it can check.
  2. Have them remove any setting that skips certificate checks, sends traffic through a proxy, or acts as a different user. Those settings hide who the cluster really is, or who you are acting as, so SMTO won't trust the route.
  3. Have them give the cluster's certificate in one place only, either inside the settings file or as a separate file, not both. Two certificate sources could disagree, so SMTO can't tell which one to trust.
  4. Then ask the agent to run a read-only command such as kubectl get pods. A successful read-only command lets SMTO record the verified cluster.

What success looks like

  • The read-only command succeeds and SMTO keeps using that cluster in later steps of the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Kubernetes access. Don't turn off certificate checking to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Kubeconfig trust routing was rejected: the server is not a valid https URL, insecure-skip-tls-verify or proxy-url is set, the user is missing or uses impersonation (as, as-uid, as-groups, as-user-extra), both certificate-authority and certificate-authority-data are set, or the CA bundle is not 1–32 PEM certificates only.

What this means

  • Trust routing rejects an unsupported user/proxy/impersonation route, insecure or malformed endpoint, conflicting CA sources, unsupported trust mode or invalid public certificate bundle. These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.

Why this can happen

  • Trust routing rejects an unsupported user/proxy/impersonation route, insecure or malformed endpoint, conflicting CA sources, unsupported trust mode or invalid public certificate bundle.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish unsupported routing/CA shape from a certificate failure; this definition does not prove a remote TLS handshake occurred.

How to fix it

  • Fix the selected context's cluster and user in the Gateway node's kubeconfig: use an https:// server, remove insecure-skip-tls-verify, proxy-url and impersonation fields, set at most one of certificate-authority or certificate-authority-data (neither means system trust), and make the CA contain only PEM certificates. Never disable certificate verification to make this pass.
  • Correct the identified trust or authentication route using supported verified HTTPS and one valid CA source or system trust; preserve certificate verification.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported discovery establishes the intended HTTPS cluster using an unambiguous verified trust route.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.

Technical notes

  • These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
